html:
The founding in 118 BCE of Narbo Martius, now Narbonne in southern France, as a colony of Roman citizens. It was Rome's first colony in Gaul.

Rome had been drawn into southern Gaul to protect its ally Massalia (Marseille) and to secure the land route to Spain. The new Via Domitia ran along the coast from the Alps to the Pyrenees, and Narbo sat on it, near the sea. Colonies outside Italy were still controversial; Gaius Gracchus had tried one at Carthage only a few years before.

Narbo grew into the main city of the province that came to be called Gallia Narbonensis. Romans simply called it "the Province", which survives as the name Provence. The colony was a base when the Cimbri swept through Gaul, and later for Julius Caesar before the Gallic Wars. Caesar settled veterans of his Tenth Legion there in 45 BCE.
sum: The founding in 118 BCE of Narbo Martius, now Narbonne in southern France, as a colony of Roman citizens. It was Rome's first colony in Gaul.
